# Revised Candidate Approach — product-1 quest (TELOS v0.3.0 / PYLAE Gate v1)

Branched from `main @ fc0fa05`. Governing pre-review: `docs/institutional-memory/iliad/PRE-REVIEWS/2026-08-27-product-1.json`. Convergence submits this approach for authorization; it does not grant implementation authority.

## 1. Objective and boundary

Close all 10 release blockers and 7 governance corrections, freeze the Phase-0 product contract, ship Phase-1a distribution, repair the normative authority chain, and release PYLAE Gate v1 as v0.3.0 from the exact qualified and accepted commit.

The v1 product is a local single-user CLI. Identity, multi-tenancy, and clustered runtime are out of scope through signed ADR PD-001 and machine-enforced product-boundary tests. Auth0 over OIDC remains the recorded Phase-1b identity decision under `product-1-ruling-identity-provider`; no v1 implementation depends on it. Phase-1b and later obligations remain scheduled in the committed readiness register.

Before implementation, run the applicable comprehension gate and `verify-contracts.mjs`, record the controlling plan SHA-256 and authorization identifiers, and obtain the Eye's authorization. Every enforcement-changing slice requires signed required-seat review and a fail-closed regression test.

## 2. Enforcement changes

### E1 — Hestia merge authority and attestation

Separate model work from merge authority. Fix and review agents receive no merge-capable credential, no OIDC permission, and no token able to bypass repository rulesets. They may push only namespaced run branches through a scoped installation token. Protected-branch rules require the deterministic Hestia qualification check and prevent direct default-branch updates or merges by that installation.

A deterministic controller, in a separate job with no model or marketplace-plugin code, derives candidates from GitHub API state and the run's server-recorded branch namespace. It validates repository identity, PR number, immutable head SHA, required checks, residue status, and merge eligibility before calling the merge API with the expected-head SHA. A 409 or any changed head is terminal `head-moved`; the controller never refreshes and retries.

`workflows/tools/attest-merges.mjs` independently queries GitHub after each attempted merge and emits `{pr, head_sha, merged, merge_commit_sha, verified_by}`. Its coverage is derived from repository state and the protected run namespace, not agent-reported arrays or agent-provided timestamps. It compares the namespace's complete before/after PR snapshot, the controller request journal, and every changed PR in the run. Any unjournaled merge, omitted candidate, blocked or excluded merge, foreign repository, SHA divergence, incomplete query, or API failure exits 2. Workflow `merged[]` remains advisory; only the deterministic attestation is merge evidence.

Acceptance includes eight adversarial workflow fixtures, fabricated agreement by both model agents, omitted-agent-output and omitted-branch fixtures, changed-head and API-failure fixtures, an attempted unauthorized merge proving repository rules block it, and a clean-run attestation fixture.

### E2 — ai-native-memory freshness and externally anchored authority

`ai-native-memory/scripts/gate.mjs` re-derives every expected answer from `derived_from` at gate time and denies missing, dangling, stale, escaped, symlinked, or unanchored inputs with distinct reason codes. Authority paths are confined to the plugin directory.

The trust root may not be supplied by mutable files inside the same tree it authenticates. The gate requires an external expected digest: in CI and a checkout this is the authority blob digest read from the trusted exact Git commit supplied by the runner; in a signed source release it is the authority digest recorded in the signed release manifest and provenance. Absence or mismatch is `trust-root-unpinned`. The externally pinned authority enumerates the admissible content-addressed record set. Each source must have a valid recomputed address and a complete hash path to that root. Editing source, expected answer, response, maps, and `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json` together therefore still breaks the external root.

Acceptance covers source-only mutation, full-lockstep mutation including mutable registry surfaces, missing external root, unanchored source, path escape, symlink escape, and a granted dogfood gate using the CI commit anchor.

### E3 — complete memory audit

Extract byte-stable freshness logic to `scripts/lib/freshness.mjs`. Recognize a direct memory-root argument through its marker predicate. Zero discovered sets exits 2 unless the explicitly advisory `--allow-empty` option is supplied. Validate all eight `RECORD_SET_LAYOUT` kinds. Decision Markdown uses the front-matter enum only. Preserve AM-40, AM-41, and AM-42 bytes; supersede legacy nonconforming records with new content-addressed records and no allowlist.

Acceptance includes direct-root discovery, zero-set failure, one failing fixture for every record kind, unchanged pinned historical bytes, supersessor validation, and a green dogfood audit.

### E4 — signed production gate

After computing the signed state, enforce: production plus unsigned blocks; production plus `allow_unsigned` blocks; unsigned without explicit opt-in blocks; and signed plus unsigned opt-in blocks as contradictory. Include profile and unsigned opt-in in headline checks. Update the nine unset-trust-mode dossiers and two advisory examples to opt in explicitly without altering production semantics.

Acceptance includes production signed and unsigned fixtures, contradiction fixtures, legacy opt-in fixtures, and the complete gate and stress suites.

### E5 — normative authority-chain repair

Create reviewed, content-addressed NORMATIVE-CURRENT successors for Multi-Model Agentic Build Gate and Claude-Led Multi-Model Prototype Workflow. Preserve the draft files unchanged as historical provenance. Mark Claude-Grok-Agy Hierarchical Agentic Workflow historical/superseded and redirect every governing citation away from it.

Add the invariant that every current normative citation terminates in a reviewed NORMATIVE-CURRENT record. Historical references are accepted only when explicitly typed non-governing provenance. Strengthen `verify-contracts.mjs` to reject governing references to draft, historical, missing, hash-mismatched, or superseded records. Redirect root invariants, loadout contracts, capability packets, comprehension queries, and gate required-doc references. The ai-native-memory plugin receives a self-contained authority record and no path outside its package boundary.

### E6 — enrollment, root invariants, and discriminating oracles

Replace `some()` enrollment checks with bijective uniqueness checks over roots, authorization IDs, and enrollment-run IDs. Sweep root `INVARIANTS.json`. Reword the zero-runtime-dependency invariant with a machine-readable flagship exception and run it against every tracked package manifest.

Every NORMATIVE record receives a structured executable oracle with both positive and negative invocations. `run-oracles.mjs` executes every declared oracle directly with bounded timeouts:

- `file` runs the exact Node entrypoint for positive and planted-violation cases.
- `npm-script` runs the exact declared package script, not merely another script from the same CI matrix entry, and then runs its declared violating fixture. Missing scripts, skipped scripts, or an `--if-present` path fail.
- `evidence-dir` runs a shared content-address validator over the real directory and a mutated temporary fixture that must be rejected.

Positive nonzero, timeout, missing, or unrunnable results fail distinctly. A negative invocation returning zero fails `oracle-nondiscriminating`. CI-matrix coverage is checked independently but never substitutes for execution.

Acceptance includes constant-success file and npm-script oracles, an npm script present in a matrix package but never invoked by that matrix, timeout and missing cases, corrupt evidence fixtures, duplicate enrollment fixtures, a planted root dependency violation, and green `verify-contracts` plus `run-oracles` CI jobs.

## 3. Governance ceremony

Run one live re-authorization council at `docs/runs/product-authorization-1/`, build ID `iliad-product-1-authz`, with signed claude/agy/codex seats and advisory grok/gemini seats. It authorizes both the AM-42 enrollment-flip regularization and AM-43 classification of `cli/` and `connectors/meta-ads-mcp/` under `PACKAGE_ROOTS_EXCLUDE`.

AM-42 remains byte-identical. AM-43 is a new independently content-addressed decision. Mutable registries record AM-42's retroactive ratification by AM-43; the new deviation record pins the AM-42 digest. Update the eight coordinated pinned surfaces together using write-then-hash-then-pin sequencing. Acceptance requires an AUTHORIZED summary and green enrollment and deferred-equality verification.

## 4. Phase-0 contract and Phase-1a distribution

Register PYLAE through the governed vocabulary lifecycle or an authorized product-brand carve-out. Create `docs/institutional-memory/product/` with PD-001 through PD-007, product glossary, state and topology decisions, naming/versioning/publish contract, `product-version.json`, and a committed machine-readable production-readiness register. The rendered readiness document is checked for drift. Every item has priority, phase, status, owner, pinned ADR, evidence, and target round; N/A requires a signed ADR. The go-live P0 gate is reporting-only until separately authorized for enforcement.

Rename v4-build-gate, v4-forge, and v4-breakout to `telos-*`; align all package and plugin versions to 0.3.0; preserve the verifier-pinned flagship package name; and do not add a root package manifest. Reconcile tracked, non-historical Node requirements to Node >=22.12.0 with a regression-tested scanner.

The private `cli/` package exposes the `pylae` bin with init, doctor, version, and verify commands. Every helper path resolves under the detected installation root, never the caller's working directory. The no-network-listener oracle scans the complete shipped product execution closure, including CLI entrypoints and spawned in-tree helpers, rather than `cli/` alone.

The supported source-release modes are explicit:

- Checkout mode requires a non-shallow Git checkout, validates the exact HEAD, and reports the commit from Git.
- Archive mode requires a release produced by `git archive`. A tracked export-substitution template and `.gitattributes` embed the source commit and authority-root digest into the archive. `pylae version` reads that immutable archive metadata, and `doctor` validates the archive manifest and required files without claiming that a Git history exists.

Thus the archive clean-room test does not require impossible `.git` history. `verify --offline-checks` validates all checks meaningful without network or Git history. Checkout-only checks report a typed not-applicable result in archive mode, while missing or inconsistent archive metadata is fatal. `npm pack cli` is only a component artifact and its README states that it requires a matching source tree.

Release clean-room acceptance extracts the source archive outside every checkout, runs doctor, version, and offline verification, asserts the embedded commit equals the release commit, and fails after deletion or substitution of any required helper.

For Meta Ads, add a manifest, CI, hermetic tests, setup documentation, environment-surface registration, a default-off kill switch, strict closed grammars for all path IDs and kinds before token access, and bounded integer parsing with a fixed hard ceiling. Missing, infinite, malformed, zero, negative, or oversized budgets fail at startup.

## 5. Freshness, release, deployment, and flagship

Add `--exact-head` to the weave runner: live HEAD must equal the recorded input head, the worktree must be clean, and every source reference must resolve under that head. Always emit freshness and head-equality fields with distinct fatal codes. Release qualification runs this mode.

`release.yml` verifies an annotated signed tag in an isolated temporary GPG home containing only the committed release public key. It checks the exact signer fingerprint recorded by PD-006, tag object type, tag target, and required-CI allowlist at that target SHA. Unknown keys, ambiguous signatures, unsigned tags, stale checks, or the release workflow counting itself as required CI fail.

Build the CLI component and source archive twice and compare bytes. Produce checksums, SBOMs, and provenance for every allowlisted artifact. Publish only a literal closed asset set; afterward require exact equality with the remote asset list and verify provenance for every remote asset. The workflow also verifies the repository's immutable-release setting through the API before publishing. Correction and key-rotation procedures live in RELEASING.md.

Pages deployment consumes only the exact successful main-push CI workflow run, downloads its SHA-named artifact by workflow-run ID, and verifies the embedded SHA before deployment. PR and non-main fixtures must not deploy. Only `demo/` is deployed; flagship deployment remains a scheduled register item.

The review marketplace action is pinned to an owner-controlled, reviewed commit and its downloaded plugin tree is hash-inventoried. It runs in a read-only job with no PR-write, contents-write, OIDC, OAuth subscription token, or repository secret. Any deterministic comment or label update occurs in a separate minimal-permission job that consumes a schema-validated artifact and executes no marketplace or model-provided code. Permission and credential-isolation fixtures fail if the review job regains any forbidden capability.

For the flagship, add a paint error boundary preserving the DOM story; responsive behavior at 375×667 with only the stage region scrolling; correct tab roles and roving keyboard focus; WCAG 2 A/AA axe coverage in both views and themes; fail-closed malformed-signature handling; and all 13 OFL license texts plus third-party notices. Each enforcement change receives its own regression test.

## 6. Delivery order and acceptance

Deliver bounded slices in this order: freshness; plugin self-containment and externally anchored E2; E3; E1 credential separation and attestation; E6; E4; product records and ADRs; naming and versions; the combined authorization ceremony with AM-43, CLI, Meta Ads, and coordinated pinned updates; release, Pages, and review-action isolation; flagship, demo, and fonts; E5 successors and citation redirects; then one train-end re-weave and Eye re-audit.

Each slice records deterministic checks, signed review where required, Eye acceptance, and an Argo ledger entry. The final head must pass comprehension, package suites, `verify-contracts`, `run-oracles`, self-weave, exact-head committed verification, release clean-room tests, release gate tests, and citation-chain verification. Release v0.3.0 only from that qualified accepted commit with required CI passing.

The retrospective and readiness register must exist before delivery is declared. Live councils prove provenance, not correctness. Phase-1b capabilities remain non-claims. No model council grants production authority; the Eye and deterministic gates remain the trust roots.
